### Shape

#### Description

A form titled "Import Project", with a close button, laid out as the [NewProjectScope](../new-project/index.md#new-project-scope)'s form is, two columns of equal width, and along the bottom a "Cancel" button and a primary "Import" button. It holds the same fields as a new project's, each looking and checked just as it does there, but for where the project is: in place of the Name field and the Location row, a "Folder" row, at the top of the first column, beneath which come the Git checkbox, the spec, code, and shape roots, and, in the second column, the template and the agents. The folder's Browse button has focus when the form opens.

#### Folder

A "Folder" row showing the existing folder to import, with a "Browse…" button beside it, empty to start with, reading "Choose a folder", muted. Browse opens a [FolderBrowserScope](../../ui/components/folder-browser/index.md#folder-browser-scope) in place of the form, titled "Choose the folder to import", starting in the folder holding the open project, or the user's home folder when no project is open. Choosing a folder makes it the folder, and choosing or cancelling goes back to the form, just as it was left. Beneath the row, muted, the folder's full path. The project's name, which names its config's anchor as a new project's name does, is the folder's name.
A folder that already holds a piton.config.pi is already a project, and can't be imported: the row says so beneath it, with an "Open it instead" link that opens it as the [OpenProjectScope](../project/open-project/index.md#open-project-scope) would and closes the form. A folder the user can't write to says that instead.

#### Defaults

Once a folder is chosen, the fields start from what is in it, and what has been typed in a field since is kept when another folder is chosen. The spec root starts as ./spec. The code root starts as ./src where the folder has a src folder, and as ./, the folder itself, where it doesn't, since an imported codebase's code is most often all of it. The shape root starts as ./spec/shape. "Initialize a Git repository" starts checked where the folder isn't in a Git repository. Where it is, whether it is the top of one or a folder within one, as `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` run in it finds, the checkbox is unchecked and disabled, and reads "Already a Git repository", its tooltip naming the repository's top folder, so an existing repository can never be initialized again. The template and the agents start as a new project's do.
The roots are written and checked as a new project's are, but the code root may be ./, the folder itself, holding the spec root, as the project's locations allow. A root that already exists in the folder is used as it is, and says so beneath its field, muted, "Uses the existing folder".

#### Importing

"Import" is disabled, with a tooltip saying why, until a folder that can be imported is chosen, the paths are valid, and an agent is checked, and while it is importing.
Pressing it writes the folder's piton.config.pi, just as a new project's config is written, named after the folder, with its roots and an adapter for each checked agent, and opencode.json as a new project writes it, unless there is one. It creates the spec root, the code root, and any shape root where they aren't there, and writes the chosen template's files into the spec root, each only where no file of that name is there already, or an empty index.pi where the template gives none and the spec root has no index.pi. It never overwrites, moves, renames, or deletes anything already in the

##### Folder

the folder's own files, its code, and anything already in a

root are left exactly as they were, and nothing outside the folder is touched.
With "Initialize a Git repository" checked, once the rest is written the folder is made a Git repository with `git init`, as a new project's is, and nothing is committed. Just before, the folder is checked again, and where it is in a Git repository by then, the top of one or within one, `git init` is never run, whatever the checkbox

##### Said

an existing repository is never initialized again, nor a new

one nested inside it, and its history, branches, index, hooks, and configuration are left exactly as they were. Whether or not Git was just initialized, where the folder is in a Git repository, a .gitignore in the folder is given the lines ignoring what Suspense keeps for this machine alone, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says: written as a new project's is where there is none, and where there is one, only the lines it lacks are added at its end, beneath a "# Suspense" comment, the rest of the file left as it was. If Git fails, the project still opens, and a warning notification says the repository couldn't be initialized, and why.
Everything it creates belongs to the user, as the [ApplicationScope](../application/index.md#application-scope) says. Once imported, the project opens as if opened with the [OpenProjectScope](../project/open-project/index.md#open-project-scope), becoming the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), and the form closes. If anything fails, the form stays open and says what went wrong above its buttons, and nothing it wrote before the failure is left half done: the piton.config.pi is written after every other file it writes, so a folder whose import failed is never taken for a project.
